parts.text:
2
Physical quantities can be classed as vectors or as scalars.
Which pair of quantities consists of two vectors?
A
kinetic energy and force
B
momentum and time
C
velocity and electric field strength
D
weight and temperature

hints: Recall that a vector needs both magnitude and direction, while a scalar needs magnitude only - test each named quantity against this.
Check kinetic energy, time and temperature in options A, B and D - none of these has a direction associated with it.
Check velocity for direction of motion and electric field strength for direction of the force on a positive charge.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: a vector quantity is fully specified only by magnitude and direction, a scalar by magnitude alone.
Test option A: kinetic energy $= \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ depends on speed squared and has no direction, so it is a scalar, while force needs a line of action and is a vector.
Test option B: momentum $= mv$ acts in the direction of velocity and is a vector, but time flows with magnitude only and is a scalar.
Test option D: weight $= mg$ acts vertically downward and is a vector, but temperature has a value in $\text{K}$ or $^{\circ}\text{C}$ with no direction and is a scalar.
Test the remaining pair: velocity specifies speed and direction of motion, and electric field strength $E = F/q$ specifies magnitude and direction of force on a positive charge, so both are vectors.
Both quantities in that pair satisfy the vector test while every other pair contains one scalar. This is option C.

A.explanation: Kinetic energy is a scalar with magnitude only, while force is a vector, so this is a mixed pair.

B.explanation: Momentum is a vector but time has magnitude only and no direction, so time is a scalar.

C.explanation: Velocity has speed plus direction and electric field strength has magnitude plus direction of force on a positive charge, so both are vectors.

D.explanation: Weight is a vector force due to gravity but temperature has magnitude only, so temperature is a scalar.
